skillSays: Start from context: which screen, what the user is trying to do, how they feel, what tone and character limits apply.
Judge every string by five principles: clear, concise, consistent, useful, human.
Use fixed patterns: error = what happened + why + how to fix; empty state = what this is + why it is empty + how to start; CTAs begin with a verb and name the outcome.
Match tone to the moment: success is celebratory but not over the top, errors are empathetic and actionable.
Deliver a set format: recommended copy, three alternatives with tone and best use, a rationale, and localization notes.

changes: Each of the three messages follows its own structure (empty state, error, success) instead of one general voice
Error names the exact rows and says "Nothing was imported", answering the fear of a half-loaded file
Buttons are verb plus outcome ("Upload fixed file", "Download error report"), never "OK" or "Submit"
Adds alternatives table, rationale and localization notes (plural rules, German button width)
Opens with a stated context block (user state, tone, subject and button limits) before writing
Delivers subject line and button with three alternatives each, tagged by tone and best use
Onboarding kept to one concept: three steps and one button that repeats step 1
Adds localization notes for variables and idiomatic phrases
Blurbs lead with the user outcome ("Patients book themselves") rather than the feature name
CTA is a verb plus what you get ("Start free trial"); "Learn more" and "Get started" are avoided
Gives three headline options with tone and channel fit, plus rationale and localization notes for "diary" and "no-shows"
